[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Infinite Inversions** [CF 540E · Infinite Inversions](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/540/E){rating="2100"}

After $n$ swaps, at most $2n$ positions are **touched** — anywhere else $s_p = p$ still. An infinite sequence with finitely many moved cells has finitely many inversions, because two untouched cells $p < q$ hold $p < q$: no inversion among them. So the count splits by how many endpoints are touched.

*Both touched:* at most $2n$ cells — count with A2's Fenwick over **compressed values**, scanning by position ("how many earlier touched values are larger", the @sec-coord-a2 pattern verbatim).

*One touched:* a touched cell at position $p$ holding value $v$ forms an inversion with every untouched $q$ strictly between $p$ and $v$ — if $v > p$, the pairs are $(p, q)$ with $p < q < v$ and $q = s_q < v = s_p$; if $v < p$, the pairs are $(q, p)$ with $v < q < p$. The untouched cells in an interval are "its length minus the touched cells it contains", and with touched **positions** sorted, two bisects price each interval in $O(\log n)$. (Two intervals, $v > p$ and $v < p$, are disjoint — no pair is ever counted twice.)

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p1-invinfinite.]{.card-link}

:::
